title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 4
paragraphs: Up to this point, the Persians say, only women had been carried off on both sides, but now the Hellenes were very greatly to blame, because they were the first to make war, launching an expedition into Asia before the barbarians had launched any into Europe. In their view, it is wrong to carry off women by force, but foolish to take it so much to heart as to seek revenge for the abduction — the sensible thing is to ignore it, since obviously no woman is ever carried off unless she is willing to go. The Persians say that they, the peoples of Asia, paid no attention at all when their own women were taken, while the Hellenes, on account of a single woman from Lacedaemon, gathered a great army, crossed into Asia, and destroyed the kingdom of Priam. From that time on, they have always regarded the Hellenic race as their enemy. For the Persians claim Asia and the barbarian peoples who live there as their own, while Europe and the Hellenes they consider a thing apart.
